summary: Nintendo and Tsunku's rhythm-minigame series, built around audio-first timing challenges across handhelds, Wii, and the upcoming Switch entry.

entries.title: Rhythm Tengoku
entries.definitive_edition: Original Japanese Game Boy Advance release

emulation.emulator: mGBA for GBA; MAME/Naomi-capable arcade emulation for arcade comparison
emulation.notes: Use GBA for the complete main run and arcade emulation only for Tempo-Up comparison.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: GBA original resolution for the complete version; arcade Naomi presentation for the secondary variants.

primary.why: The GBA release is the complete original version, with the 48 rhythm games plus Endless Games and Rhythm Toys; the arcade version has better cabinet presentation but fewer regular extras.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Japanese GBA cartridge on GBA/DS hardware or via mGBA for capture. Use the arcade release only to sample its Tempo-Up versions.

secondary.exclusive_content: The Sega Naomi arcade release adds Tempo-Up versions of the first six games but lacks the GBA release's Endless Games and Rhythm Toys.
secondary.what_to_play: Sample the arcade Tempo-Up versions after the GBA main run.
secondary.why: The arcade release has a limited regular-game set and Tempo-Up additions.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official modern remaster is documented.

entries.title: Rhythm Heaven

emulation.notes: Emulation helps capture; original DS hardware best preserves flick/touch input.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: DS-resolution 2D presentation with emulator scaling for capture.

primary.why: The DS entry was released on Nintendo DS with touch-screen flick, tap, and slide controls and no documented official port, so the original cartridge is the complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the original DS cartridge on DS hardware for touch timing. Use melonDS or DeSmuME only for capture convenience.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official remaster or port is documented.

entries.title: Rhythm Heaven Fever

emulation.notes: Dolphin can improve capture clarity, but rhythm latency should be tested carefully.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Wii presentation upscaled through emulator or Wii U output.

primary.why: Rhythm Heaven Fever was built around Wii Remote A/B button timing and the original Wii release remains the complete official version; the Wii U release is a later Wii Virtual Console route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Wii disc on Wii or Wii U hardware for original controls. Use Dolphin for clean capture/upscaling if latency is configured carefully.

entries.remaster_caveats: The Wii U release is a Wii Virtual Console release, not a remaster.

entries.title: Rhythm Heaven Megamix

emulation.notes: Use original hardware for normal play; emulator capture can help video output.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: 3DS presentation with emulator scaling for capture.

primary.why: Megamix is the fourth Rhythm Heaven entry on Nintendo 3DS and functions as a large compilation with previous-game stages plus new games, shortened versions, Endless Games, and remixes.
primary.how_to_play: Play the original 3DS release on 3DS hardware for the complete official package. Use 3DS emulation only for capture if legally configured.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official remaster or port is documented.

entries.title: Rhythm Heaven Groove

emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Nintendo Switch release, with Nintendo Switch 2 compatibility marked supported by Nintendo.

primary.why: Rhythm Heaven Groove is a Nintendo Switch release with Nintendo Switch 2 compatibility support and a July 2, 2026 release date.
primary.how_to_play: As of June 22, 2026, wait for the July 2, 2026 launch, then play the Nintendo Switch release; Switch 2 compatibility is supported with behavior consistent with Switch.

entries.remaster_caveats: Pre-release entry as of June 22, 2026; revisit after launch for patches or platform-specific differences.
